Description: Build 42 no longer prints joins and leaves to the console, so AMP shows 0 players. This is on by default: the server starts with the game's detailed log, which prints a line for each join and leave. AMP then shows who is online, the kick and ban buttons work, and AMP's 'last player leaves' tasks work. The detailed log also prints player IP addresses and RCON passwords; this template hides both in AMP's console, but the game's own server-console.txt file still has them, so only give file access to people you trust. It also adds some extra lines to the console.

Sent to everyone in game whenever the server reports that a Workshop mod has an update. The server only checks when it is told to: in AMP, open Schedule and add a task that sends the console command checkModsNeedUpdate every 10 or 15 minutes. Then restart when it suits you (players with the new version cannot join until the server restarts). Leave empty to send no message.
DefaultValue: A mod has been updated. The server will restart soon to install it.

Description: Start here. Set this before the first start: the server won't start without it. This is the password for your in-game admin account (the username below), not the one players use to join. The game resets the admin account to this password every time the server starts, so this box always holds the real password. Change settings here rather than in the game's files, because AMP rewrites those files from these boxes every time the server starts. Each box saves when you click away from it and takes effect after a restart, so it's safe to change one while the server is running. You can also change sandbox settings in the game's admin menu: see 'Sandbox changes made in game' at the top of the World tab. Mod sandbox settings aren't in AMP. Change them in the game's admin menu or the Manage Settings editor (see the World tab). AMP never overwrites them. Use a password you don't use anywhere else: anyone you give access to this server in AMP may be able to see it.
The name of your in-game admin account. The game creates it on the first start.

The name the game uses for this server's settings files and world. Changing this starts a brand new world with fresh settings files. The old world stays on disk under its old name. Use letters, numbers, dashes or underscores only.

The most memory (RAM) the server can use. It starts at 3072 MB (3 GB), the same as the game's own server launcher. For Build 42 we recommend at least 10240 MB (10 GB), adjusted for the mods you run. The game's memory manager grows towards this limit whether it needs the memory or not, so leave enough for Windows and anything else running on the machine. If the console shows OutOfMemoryError, raise this.

Presets and mods' sandbox settings: use the game's own settings editor. On your PC, open Project Zomboid, click HOST, then Manage settings, then Create New Settings (or Edit Selected Settings). Name the settings the same as this server's save name so nothing needs renaming. Choose the same mods as this server, use Apply Preset if you want a preset, change any setting, game or mod, and save. The game saves it in the Zomboid\Server folder in your user folder. Stop this server, then in the File Manager upload only the saved servertest_SandboxVars.lua (your save name in place of servertest) to Zomboid/Server, replacing the old one, and start. Leave the .ini it also saves: AMP's own boxes set those settings. With Last change wins the uploaded settings are kept; with AMP always wins, AMP's sandbox boxes replace them. Then import as described below so these boxes match. This setting decides who wins when a sandbox setting (zombies, loot, world and so on) is changed both here and in the game's admin menu. Last change wins: at each start, only the boxes you changed here since the last start are applied; everything else keeps the game's value, including changes made in game. AMP always wins: every sandbox box is applied at each start, so in-game changes last until the next restart. Mods' own sandbox settings are always kept, whichever you pick. To make these boxes show what the game is really using (after changes in game, or after bringing in an existing world): start the server once, then in the File Manager right click Zomboid/Server/servertest_SandboxImport.ini (your save name in place of servertest) and choose Import. That file is refreshed at every start. An existing world is safe: on its first start here, nothing from AMP is applied to it until you import or change a box.
ZGC is what the game's own launcher uses on Windows 10 and later. G1GC uses less memory up front and suits older systems.
Added to the Java part of the start command. Leave empty unless a guide tells you what to add.
Added to the end of the start command, for example -ip 192.168.1.10 to bind one network address. Leave empty unless you need it.

RCON lets other programs, like a Discord bot or an admin tool, send commands to the server using the RCON password (set in Start here). When this is on, only programs on this server machine can use RCON, so nothing on your network or the internet can reach it. Turn it off only if a program on another machine needs RCON, and keep the RCON port closed on your router.

Build 42 is the game's normal Steam version. Unstable gets test builds first; players must be on the same version to join. After changing this, stop the server, click Update, then start it. Build 41 worlds do not load in Build 42. Mods do not go in AMP's own Steam Workshop box on this page: that box causes a Steam login loop. Add mods in Configuration, Server, Mods and map.

When on, anyone can join; their account is created the first time they log in with a password. When off, only people already on the whitelist (or allowed Steam IDs) can get in. Tip: The Indie Stone's B42 multiplayer notes suggest whitelisted servers, so Open off. In the settings file: Open.
The message shown in chat right after a player logs in. Use <LINE> for a new line and <RGB:1,0,0> for colour. In the settings file: ServerWelcomeMessage.
DefaultValue: Welcome to Project Zomboid Multiplayer! <LINE> <LINE> To interact with the Chat panel: press Tab, T, or Enter. <LINE> <LINE> The Tab key will change the target stream of the message. <LINE> <LINE> Global Streams: /all <LINE> Local Streams: /say, /yell <LINE> Special Steams: /whisper, /safehouse, /faction. <LINE> <LINE> Press the Up arrow to cycle through your message history. Click the Gear icon to customize chat. <LINE> <LINE> Happy surviving!

Description: When on, new logins are refused with 'Server is too busy' while the server is dropping network packets. In the settings file: DenyLoginOnOverloadedServer.

How many players can be on at once. When full, new joiners are refused with 'ServerFull' (or wait in the queue if the login queue is on). Tip: The Indie Stone's B42 notes suggest 20 players or fewer. In the settings file: MaxPlayers.
Players whose ping (in milliseconds) stays above this are kicked. 0 turns it off. Staff with the right permission are never kicked for lag. In the settings file: PingLimit.

DisplayName: Drop Off White List After Death
Description: When on, a player's account is removed from the whitelist when their character dies, so on a closed (Open off) server they cannot come back without an admin. In the settings file: DropOffWhiteListAfterDeath.
A password everyone must type to join. Leave empty for no password. A /reloadoptions applies a new password without a restart. In the settings file: Password.
Limits how many different accounts one Steam user can create here. 0 means no limit. Only checked when the server runs in Steam mode. In the settings file: MaxAccountsPerUser.
When on, a player can bring extra split-screen players on the same PC. When off, only the first player on each PC can join. In the settings file: AllowCoop.
When on, players joining a busy or full server wait in a queue instead of being refused. Staff with priority login skip ahead. In the settings file: LoginQueueEnabled.
Seconds a queued player is given to finish connecting when it is their turn, before the next person is let in. In the settings file: LoginQueueConnectTimeout.
When on, usernames may use letters outside basic English (for example Cyrillic). Checked when an account logs in. In the settings file: AllowNonAsciiUsername.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.
When on, the server is listed in the in-game public server browser. In the settings file: Public.
The server name shown in the in-game browser and the Steam browser (up to 64 characters). In the settings file: PublicName.
The description shown in the in-game public server browser (up to 256 characters). In the settings file: PublicDescription.
When on, the player list shows Steam names and avatars. In the settings file: SteamScoreboard.
When on, Steam's VAC anti-cheat is switched on for this server. A -steamvac value on the command line overrides it. In the settings file: SteamVAC.
When on, the server asks your router to open its ports automatically at start. If the server hangs at start, set this off. In the settings file: UPnP.
Forces the IP address the server announces to the public list. Only needed when the machine has more than one address. In the settings file: server_browser_announced_ip.
When on, account names show above players' heads. In the settings file: DisplayUserName.
When on, the character's first and last name show above their head. In the settings file: ShowFirstAndLastName.
When on, a player whose face is covered shows a 'disguised' name instead of their own. In the settings file: UsernameDisguises.
When on, disguised players show no name at all instead of the 'disguised' label. In the settings file: HideDisguisedUserName.
Forces every new character to start at these x,y,z map coordinates. 0,0,0 means use the normal spawn choices. In the settings file: SpawnPoint.
Items every new character starts with, as item types separated by commas, for example Base.Axe,Base.Bag_BigHikingBag. In the settings file: SpawnItems.
When on, fire is disabled in multiplayer except campfires. In the settings file: NoFire.
When on, players can smash world objects and walls with a sledgehammer. In the settings file: AllowDestructionBySledgehammer.
When on, non-admin players can only sledgehammer things inside their own safehouse. Needs AllowDestructionBySledgehammer on. In the settings file: SledgehammerOnlyInSafehouse.
When on, players can sleep in beds and cars. When everyone online is asleep, time speeds up. Tip: Commonly off on public servers. In the settings file: SleepAllowed.
When on, characters get tired and must sleep. Only works when SleepAllowed is also on. In the settings file: SleepNeeded.
When on, players can be knocked down. The game marks this as work in progress that may cause position desync. In the settings file: KnockedDownAllowed.

DisplayName: Sneak Mode Hide From Other Players
Description: When on, a sneaking player is harder for other players to see, unless they are sprinting. In the settings file: SneakModeHideFromOtherPlayers.

DisplayName: Ultra Speed Doesnot Affect To Animals
Description: When on, animals are not sped up while time runs very fast (for example while everyone sleeps). In the settings file: UltraSpeedDoesnotAffectToAnimals.
When on, a player who dies can respawn at the spot where they died. In the settings file: PlayerRespawnWithSelf.
When on, a player who dies can respawn next to a split-screen or Remote Play partner on the same PC. In the settings file: PlayerRespawnWithOther.
How much faster time runs while every online player is asleep. In the settings file: FastForwardMultiplier.
The most items one container can hold, counting every small item such as each nail. 0 means no limit. In the settings file: ItemNumbersLimitPerContainer.

DisplayName: Remove Player Corpses On Corpse Removal
Description: When on, dead players' bodies are also removed when the sandbox corpse removal timer (HoursForCorpseRemoval) clears bodies. In the settings file: RemovePlayerCorpsesOnCorpseRemoval.
When on, players get a 'delete all' button on bins. In the settings file: TrashDeleteAll.

DisplayName: Mouse Over To See Display Name
Description: When on, you only see another player's name when you point your mouse at them. In the settings file: MouseOverToSeeDisplayName.
When on, other players behind your character are hidden, the same way zombies you cannot see are hidden. In the settings file: HidePlayersBehindYou.
When on, players running into each other bump and can knock each other over. In the settings file: PlayerBumpPlayer.

Which other players appear on the in-game map: 1 nobody, 2 faction and safehouse mates, 3 those plus players you can see, 4 everyone. Staff who can see the world map always see everyone. In the settings file: MapRemotePlayerVisibility.
When on, players see their map coordinates in the lower right corner. In the settings file: ShowCoordinates.
When on, players (and admins) can claim a building as their safehouse. In the settings file: PlayerSafehouse.
When on, only admins can claim safehouses. In the settings file: AdminSafehouse.
When on, people who are not members can walk into a safehouse. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowTrepass.
When on, fire can damage safehouses. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowFire.
When on, non-members can take items from a safehouse. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowLoot.
When on, a player who dies can respawn inside a safehouse they belonged to. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowRespawn.
In-game days a character must survive before they can claim a safehouse. 0 means straight away. In the settings file: SafehouseDaySurvivedToClaim.
Real-world hours a safehouse can go unvisited before it is removed. 0 turns removal off. In the settings file: SafeHouseRemovalTime.
When on, players can also claim shops and other non-home buildings. In the settings file: SafehouseAllowNonResidential.
When on, name disguises do not work inside safehouses. In the settings file: SafehouseDisableDisguises.
The largest area (width times height in tiles) a safezone claim may cover. 0 means no limit. In the settings file: MaxSafezoneSize.
When on, safehouse wars can happen, during which safehouse protection is lifted. In the settings file: War.
Seconds of warning before a war begins. In the settings file: WarStartDelay.
How long a war lasts, in seconds. In the settings file: WarDuration.
The safehouse hit point limit used during wars. In the settings file: WarSafehouseHitPoints.
When on, a safehouse acts like a normal house while an owner is online, so its protection only applies while they are offline. In the settings file: DisableSafehouseWhenOwnerConnected.
When on, players can create factions. In the settings file: Faction.
In-game days a character must survive before creating a faction. In the settings file: FactionDaySurvivedToCreate.
How many members a faction needs before its owner can set a name tag. In the settings file: FactionPlayersRequiredForTag.
When on, players can hurt and kill each other. Tip: Commonly off, or on with SafetySystem so PvP is opt-in. In the settings file: PVP.
When on, PvP events are reported in admin chat. In the settings file: PVPLogToolChat.
When on, PvP events are written to the server log files. In the settings file: PVPLogToolFile.

When on (and PVP is on), each player switches PvP for themselves, and a player can only be hurt when PvP is on for both sides. When off, everyone can hurt everyone. In the settings file: SafetySystem.
When on, a skull shows over players who have PvP switched on. In the settings file: ShowSafety.
How long it takes to switch your PvP mode on or off. In the settings file: SafetyToggleTimer.
How long a player must wait before switching PvP mode again; hitting another player adds to it. In the settings file: SafetyCooldownTimer.

When a player leaves while a PvP timer is still running, their character stays behind for a delay based on this value, so leaving cannot be used to escape a fight. In the settings file: SafetyDisconnectDelay.
When on, a player who has just been hit by another player can swing back straight away. In the settings file: PVPMeleeWhileHitReaction.
Damage multiplier for melee hits between players. In the settings file: PVPMeleeDamageModifier.
Damage multiplier for gun hits between players. In the settings file: PVPFirearmDamageModifier.
When on, the global /all chat channel is available. In the settings file: GlobalChat.

Which chat channels exist, as short codes separated by commas: s say, r radio, a admin, w whisper, y yell, sh safehouse, f faction, all global (only if GlobalChat is on). In the settings file: ChatStreams.
When on, a message goes to everyone in chat whenever a player dies. In the settings file: AnnounceDeath.
When on, a message goes to everyone in chat whenever an animal dies. In the settings file: AnnounceAnimalDeath.
When on, built-in voice chat is available. In the settings file: VoiceEnable.
The minimum distance in tiles for voice chat. In the settings file: VoiceMinDistance.
The furthest distance in tiles at which voice chat can be heard. In the settings file: VoiceMaxDistance.
When on, voice chat sounds come from the speaker's direction. In the settings file: Voice3D.
When on, players with any staff role cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioStaff.
When on, admins cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioAdmin.
When on, GMs cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioGM.
When on, overseers cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioOverseer.
When on, moderators cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioModerator.
When on, invisible staff cannot transmit on in-game radios. In the settings file: DisableRadioInvisible.
Path to a text file of banned words, one per line, used by the chat filter. Read once at start. In the settings file: BadWordListFile.
Path to a text file of allowed words, one per line, that the filter should not block even if they contain a banned word. Read once at start. In the settings file: GoodWordListFile.
What happens to someone who uses a banned word: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 record it. The message is still sent with the word replaced. In the settings file: BadWordPolicy.
Text that replaces a banned word in chat (up to 16 characters). In the settings file: BadWordReplacement.
The longest chat message a player can type. In the settings file: ChatMessageCharacterLimit.
Seconds a player must wait between chat messages. In the settings file: ChatMessageSlowModeTime.
When on, the server's built-in Discord bot connects and relays chat. Read when the server starts. In the settings file: DiscordEnable.
The access token of the Discord bot the server logs in as. Keep it secret; the game leaves it out of the public option list. In the settings file: DiscordToken.
The Discord channel name (not ID) for chat relay. The bot uses the first text channel with this name. In the settings file: DiscordChatChannel.
The Discord channel name (not ID) where the bot posts log messages. In the settings file: DiscordLogChannel.
The Discord channel name (not ID) where the bot listens for commands. In the settings file: DiscordCommandChannel.

A web address the server posts short messages to: when a player joins or leaves, anti-cheat reports, and when the server is opened or closed. It works with a Discord webhook with no bot: in Discord, open the channel's settings, Integrations, Webhooks, New Webhook, Copy Webhook URL, then paste it here and add /slack to the end.
Set from the ports AMP gives this instance.

Required. RCON lets other programs, like a Discord bot or an admin tool, send commands to the server using this password. Use a long password you don't use anywhere else: anyone you give access to this server in AMP may be able to see it, and the game keeps it in plain text in its settings file. By default only programs on this server machine can use RCON: see 'RCON from this machine only' in Remote admin (RCON).

The mod IDs to load, separated by semicolons, for example ModA;ModB. Each mod also needs its Workshop item number in the box below, or nothing loads. One Workshop item can hold several mod IDs; list each one you want. A backslash before an ID (\ModA) is optional: the game removes backslashes before reading this list.
The map folders to load, separated by semicolons. Map mods go first and Muldraugh, KY goes last, for example MapModA;Muldraugh, KY. This box must not be empty.
When on, players whose game or mod files do not match the server are refused. In the settings file: DoLuaChecksum.

The Steam Workshop item numbers, separated by semicolons with no spaces. Each number is at the end of the mod's Workshop page address, after id=. The game downloads these itself at start. Do not use AMP's own Steam Workshop box on the Updates page.
Saves the loaded parts of the map every this many real minutes. 0 means only the normal saving (when areas unload). In the settings file: SaveWorldEveryMinutes.
How many backup zip files of each kind to keep before old ones are deleted. In the settings file: BackupsCount.
When on, a backup is made every time the server starts. In the settings file: BackupsOnStart.
When on, a backup is made at start when the game version differs from the last run. In the settings file: BackupsOnVersionChange.
Makes a backup every this many real minutes while running. 0 turns timed backups off. In the settings file: BackupsPeriod.

The world generation seed. It is only used when the world's generation data does not exist yet. The game's tooltip says to delete map_worldgen.bin in the save to change it. Only used when a new world is created. Changing this later does nothing. In the settings file: Seed.
When on, game time stops while nobody is online. In the settings file: PauseEmpty.
Changes how the server hands control of each zombie between players' games when more than one player is online. In the settings file: SwitchZombiesOwnershipEachUpdate.

Description: No code in 42.21 reads this server setting. The sandbox setting of the same name is the one the game uses. In the settings file: BloodSplatLifespanDays.
Scales how far a running car engine draws zombies. The game says lower values can help with lag. In the settings file: CarEngineAttractionModifier.
How often, in seconds, the server gathers multiplayer statistics. 0 turns statistics off. In the settings file: MultiplayerStatisticsPeriod.
The most network messages of one kind the server accepts from each player per second. In the settings file: MaxPacketsPerSecond.
When on, the server allows ragdoll physics reactions when characters are hit. In the settings file: UsePhysicsHitReaction.
When on, everyone hears a thunder sound when a player who is online is banned or kicked. In the settings file: BanKickGlobalSound.
What the server does when it catches someone breaking the PvP safety rules: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatSafety.
What the server does when a player or vehicle moves faster than allowed: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatSpeed.
What the server does when a player walks through walls: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. Off by default. In the settings file: AntiCheatNoClip.
What the server does about impossible hits (damage, distance, weapon, vehicle hits): 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatHit.
What the server does about broken or unexpected network messages: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. Off by default. In the settings file: AntiCheatPacketException.
What the server does when someone uses powers their role does not have: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatPermission.
What the server does about impossible skill XP gains: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. The allowed amount follows the XP multiplier sandbox settings. In the settings file: AntiCheatXP.
What the server does about invalid safehouse actions (owner, member, non-member): 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatSafeHouse.
What the server does about invalid player data or targets: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatPlayer.
What the server does when a player's file check result changes during play: 1 ban, 2 kick, 3 log only, 4 off. In the settings file: AntiCheatChecksum.
When on, the player list hides other players from each player. In the settings file: DisableScoreboard.
When on, staff whose role allows hiding are left out of the player list. In the settings file: HideAdminsInPlayerList.
Which client commands are left out of (minus) or kept in (plus) the cmd.txt log, as rules like -vehicle.* and +vehicle.fixPart separated by semicolons. In the settings file: ClientCommandFilter.
Which player actions are written to the ClientActionLogs log, as action names separated by semicolons. In the settings file: ClientActionLogs.
When on, skill level changes are written to the PerkLog log. In the settings file: PerkLogs.
The top speed (km/h) for cars in multiplayer. The speed anti-cheat uses the same number for vehicles. In the settings file: SpeedLimit.
When on, players cannot tow cars with cars in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableVehicleTowing.
When on, players cannot tow trailers in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableTrailerTowing.
When on, players cannot tow burnt-out wrecks in multiplayer. In the settings file: DisableBurntTowing.
When off, no cars spawn in newly explored areas. Same in all five game presets: on. In the settings file: EnableVehicles.
How many cars spawn in newly explored areas. Game presets: Apocalypse Low, Outbreak Normal, Rising Normal, Extinction Low, Six Months Later Low. In the settings file: CarSpawnRate.
Multiplies how loud car engines are to zombies. Same in all five game presets: 1.0. In the settings file: ZombieAttractionMultiplier.
When on, cars are unlocked and need no keys to start. Same in all five game presets: off. In the settings file: VehicleEasyUse.
How full the tanks of found cars are. Game presets: Apocalypse Low, Outbreak Normal, Rising Normal, Extinction Low, Six Months Later Low. In the settings file: InitialGas.
How often found cars are locked. Game presets: Apocalypse Sometimes, Outbreak Rare, Rising Rare, Extinction Very Often, Six Months Later Never. In the settings file: LockedCar.
Multiplies how fast cars burn fuel. Game presets: Apocalypse 1.0, Outbreak 1.0, Rising 0.6, Extinction 1.0, Six Months Later 1.0. In the settings file: CarGasConsumption.
The general state of found cars' parts. Game presets: Apocalypse Normal, Outbreak Normal, Rising Normal, Extinction Low, Six Months Later Very Low. In the settings file: CarGeneralCondition.
How much damage cars take in crashes. Same in all five game presets: Normal. In the settings file: CarDamageOnImpact.
How much damage a character takes when hit by a car: none, low, normal, high or very high. Same in all five game presets: None. In the settings file: DamageToPlayerFromHitByACar.
When on, wrecked-car traffic jams appear on main roads in newly explored areas. Same in all five game presets: on. In the settings file: TrafficJam.

How often found cars have a working alarm. Only affects places nobody has visited yet; explored areas keep what they had. Game presets: Apocalypse Rare, Outbreak Rare, Rising Rare, Extinction Sometimes, Six Months Later Never. In the settings file: CarAlarm.
When on, people inside a car can be hurt when it crashes. Same in all five game presets: on. In the settings file: PlayerDamageFromCrash.
In-game hours before a wailing car siren switches itself off. 0 means it does not switch off on its own. Same in all five game presets: 0.0. In the settings file: SirenShutoffHours.
The chance a found car has any fuel at all. Game presets: Apocalypse Normal, Outbreak Normal, Rising Normal, Extinction Low, Six Months Later Low. In the settings file: ChanceHasGas.

How often you find well kept cars that a survivor looked after. Game presets: Apocalypse Low, Outbreak Normal, Rising Normal, Extinction Low, Six Months Later Low. In the settings file: RecentlySurvivorVehicles.
When on, zombies head toward car sirens. Game presets: Apocalypse on, Outbreak on, Rising on, Extinction on, Six Months Later off. In the settings file: SirenEffectsZombies.

The headline zombie amount. In the settings screens, picking it also fills in ZombieConfig.PopulationMultiplier. The game also reads this value directly for some things: how many zombies sit in rooms, map zombie density, and None switches zombie creation off. Tip: Normal is the common pick. Game presets: Apocalypse Normal, Outbreak Normal, Rising Low, Extinction High, Six Months Later Insane. In the settings file: Zombies.
Urban Focused puts more zombies in towns; Uniform spreads them evenly over the map. Same in all five game presets: Urban Focused. In the settings file: Distribution.

When on, a little randomness is added to where zombie groups are placed in generated areas. Game presets: Apocalypse on, Outbreak on, Rising on, Extinction on, Six Months Later off. In the settings file: ZombieVoronoiNoise.
